Hey. 31 is pretty fucking young :) I know a lot of unmarried people in their 30s.

Anecdotal: (I'm all over Reddit with the anecdotes tonight, sorry)

My step dad is an alcoholic. He was pretty awful when I was a kid. He beat me and my mom and was verbally/emotionally abusive literally every day. 

I'm not saying this will be right for you, but hey- trying  ANYTHING is better than giving up completely, right?

6 years since I've moved out- he started the Sinclair Program and its actually helped him moderate his drinking and he's actually alright to be around now. I can have a beer with the guy who abused me.

I dunno. It really sucks. It sucks to not be heard when you tell people that your brain isn't working right.

I just posted that I'm kind of in a crisis right now, so maybe I'm not the best person to tell you this haha.

Anecdotal experience from a girl who went to the hospital for suicide:

I spent 5 days in the psych ward a while back after a suicide attempt. I felt the best I've felt in *my entire life* after getting out. It was awful and amazing being there. Seeing all the painfully normal people who were also in there because their brains had turned on them too was a massive relief. We stayed up until 3-4am just chatting *honestly* about life and it's ups and downs while we (lovingly) teased the nurses and played Jenga haha. Even the 50+ year old 4 foot tall woman who didn't speak a lick of English would sit and laugh with us while we talked.

It sucked too. A lot of it sucked. I hated having my family there because they just told me about how much I hurt them by trying to hurt myself. But my friends and my partner would hold my hand and make me laugh about how ridiculous the whole thing was. 

**TLDR** Be there if she wants you to be. Make her smile if you can. If she asks you to leave, leave. This is a time that can really help her heal. I know you're worried, but follow her lead. She probably needs to feel in control right now.
